workflows.title: How to schedule a calendar task
workflows.purpose: Schedule a new compliance task, assign it to a team member, configure its frequency, and add it to the firm's compliance calendar.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Calendar
Click a day cell on the calendar grid to open the day details panel
Click "New Task" in the day details panel header
Enter the task name in the "Title" field
Select a due date using the date picker next to the Title field
Optionally enter task instructions in the "Description" textarea
Click the assignee dropdown and select an employee, or leave it as "Unassigned"
Click the recurrence dropdown and choose a repeat frequency (e.g. "Does not repeat", "Daily", or "Custom...")
Click "Add Task" to save and schedule the new calendar task
prerequisites: Admin-role account: task creation/edit/delete on the compliance calendar is gated server-side by has_role_access(User.Role.ADMIN) (hadrius_backend/hadrius/tasks/views.py get_post_tasks / patch_delete_task) — a non-admin viewer's task list comes back empty and cannot create tasks.
Firm Oversight module enabled for the recording tenant (feature_enabled(FIRM_OVERSIGHT) gate on the same views) — confirmed ON for company 1013 (Stephen Investments) via feature_access check.

At least one employee record if the operator wants to demonstrate assigning the task to a named person (optional — the assignee dropdown defaults to and can be left as 'Unassigned', so this is not a hard blocker).

workflows.title: How to sync the testing calendar to an external calendar
workflows.purpose: Generate and copy an iCal subscription link so scheduled compliance test deadlines automatically sync to an external calendar application (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook). The link reflects whichever entity and status filters are currently applied on the Calendar page, and excludes completed items and ad-hoc tasks regardless of filters.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Calendar.

(Optional) Use the entity dropdown next to the "Calendar" title and the "All statuses" filter dropdown above the grid to narrow to the entities and statuses you want reflected in the subscription — the sync link is generated from whatever filters are currently applied on this page.

Click "Sync calendar" in the top right of the calendar page header. This immediately generates the subscription link and opens the "Calendar sync link generated" dialog showing the "Calendar feed URL" field.

If a "Not included in this subscription" notice appears in the dialog, review it — it lists anything the current view shows that the feed will not carry (for example, ad-hoc tasks, or a status filter such as "Completed" that has no subscription equivalent).
Click "Copy link" to the left of the "Calendar feed URL" field to copy the subscription URL to your clipboard (a "Calendar sync link copied to clipboard" confirmation toast appears).

Review the "How to add to your calendar" instructions in the dialog: open your calendar app (Google Calendar, Outlook, or Apple Calendar), find its "From URL" or "By URL" option (usually under Settings or Add Calendar), then paste and confirm the copied link.
Close the dialog using the "X" close button in its top-right corner — the dialog has no "Done" button.
prerequisites: Firm Oversight / Testing program module enabled for the tenant (backend gate: feature_enabled(FIRM_OVERSIGHT))

Recording account has Firm Oversight basic access (Role.Action.FIRM_OVERSIGHT_BASIC_ACCESS) and an active Employee record in the company — the same baseline needed just to open the Calendar page, not anything extra for this workflow specifically

workflows.title: How to link a test to additional entities
workflows.purpose: Link an existing compliance test to one or more of the firm's business entities so edits and completion status stay in sync across them.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests.
Click on a test's row in the tests table to open that test's details page.
In the test details page, click the actions menu (the vertical ellipsis icon button in the top right).
Click "Link test to entity" in the actions menu.

In the "Select entities to link this test." dialog, use the search box to find an entity if needed, then turn on the toggle switch next to each entity you want to link the test to. (A toggle stays off/disabled for an entity that has no active policy covering it.)

Click "Link" to save. A confirmation toast, "Link test enabled — This test is now linked across different entities. Edits and completion will stay in sync," confirms the linked entities will stay in sync.
prerequisites: Firm Oversight admin role (FIRM_OVERSIGHT_ADMIN_ACCESS) on the recording account — the actions menu only shows "Start a new test run", "Edit test", "Change owner/reviewer", "Change due dates", "Link test to entity" and "Archive test run" when isAdmin is true (page_test_details.tsx), and the backend post_entity/link endpoints enforce the same role action.
At least one existing compliance test to open from Testing program > Tests.

At least two business entities in the firm, where at least one entity other than the test's current entity has an active policy/manual covering it — a toggle in the link dialog is disabled (EntityRow disabled={!hasManual}) for any entity with no ACTIVE FirmPolicyVersion covering it, so with only one entity, or a second entity whose only policy is archived, there is nothing linkable.
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Firm oversight > Overview (entities section).
Click "Add entity".
Enter an optional name suffix and select an entity type from the "Entity tag" dropdown.

Click "Save" without attaching a document — the backend always creates a default policy and an ACTIVE first version for the new entity in the same request (service_manual_entities.create_policy + create_version, entities.py post_entity), so the entity is immediately eligible to be toggled on in the link dialog even with no WSP upload.
Return to Testing program > Tests and open the test you want to link, to confirm the new entity now appears as a toggle-enabled option in the "Link test to entity" dialog.

workflows.title: How to link a control to a policy section
workflows.purpose: Open a policy document, narrow it to a specific section, and link an existing compliance control to that section from the section's controls panel.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies
Click on a policy row in the list to open the policy details view.
In the left "Sections" panel, click the desired section to select it (the document scrolls to that section).
Click "Show only this section" beneath the Sections list to narrow the document to that section.
In the right-hand panel, now titled "Controls in this section," review the section's currently linked controls.
Click "Link control" to open the "Link a control to this section" dialog.
Choose the desired control from the "Select a control" dropdown.
Click "Link control" in the dialog to confirm and attach the control to the section.
prerequisites: A policy (compliance manual) whose document actually has parsed headings, so the left 'Sections' panel renders — a policy with no detected headings shows no Sections panel at all and the flow cannot start.

That same policy must already have at least one control associated with it at the policy level (the set shown by Testing program > Controls filtered to that policy) — the 'Link control' dropdown only offers controls already tied to the policy as a whole, filtered down to ones not yet linked to the selected section; a policy with zero controls disables the 'Link control' button entirely ('Every control is already linked here' / nothing to choose).

The policy must be opened at its current/active version, not an older archived version — the backend rejects section-control writes on a non-ACTIVE FirmPolicyVersion and the UI marks the panel read-only in that case.

The recording account needs the Firm Oversight feature enabled for the tenant and the FIRM_OVERSIGHT_ADMIN_ACCESS role action, since GET/POST/DELETE on section-control links all require it (views_section_controls.py) — this is the same permission the rest of the Testing program module needs, so it is presumably already satisfied for whatever account records these workflows.
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies.
Click a policy row and confirm a left 'Sections' panel appears with at least one section listed; if it says 'No sections found' or shows no panel, go back and pick a different policy row instead.

In the right-hand controls area, confirm the policy already shows at least one associated control (visible once you select and narrow to a section, in the 'Controls in this section' panel's 'Link control' dialog dropdown). If the dropdown is empty and 'Link control' is disabled for every section, this policy has no controls at all — pick a different policy that does.

If no policy on hand has any associated controls, navigate to Testing program > Controls, click the control-creation button (e.g. '+ Create control'), and set the new control's policy/manual field to the target policy before saving, so it becomes available to link at the section level.

workflows.title: How to export all of an entity's testing data
workflows.purpose: Request a bundled, company-wide export of the testing program's tests, risks, and controls for a chosen date range, then retrieve the finished archive from Settings > Exports.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests.
On the entity's Tests page, click "Export" (Download icon) in the top right corner of the page header.

In the "Export testing program" dialog, set the "Start date" and "End date" fields to the desired range, or click one of the preset buttons — "YTD", "Last quarter", or "Last month" — to fill them automatically. Note this exports the whole testing program company-wide, not just the entity you launched it from.
Click "Prepare export" to queue the export job.
A "Preparing your export" confirmation toast appears. Click "Open export" in the toast to go to that export's detail page under Settings > Exports.
Once the export finishes building its files, download the archive using the "Download" button on each part (or "Download all" when there is more than one part).
prerequisites: Admin role for the recording account — confirmed in backend tests (hadrius_backend/hadrius/tests/firm_oversight/test_permissions.py::test_employee_cannot_export_the_firms_comprehensive_report and tests/common/test_not_an_employee_403.py) that POST /company/{id}/firm_oversight/export/ returns 403 for a plain employee; only an admin can queue this export.

The recording account must also be a registered active employee of the company (a roles_employee row) — an admin login with no Employee record for this company also gets refused (test_not_an_employee_403.py), so make sure the demo admin used is properly onboarded as staff of Stephen Investments, not just holding an admin auth role.
Testing program (firm oversight) must be enabled for the tenant — assumed already true since this whole module's other workflows depend on it; not something to set up specially.

Live-verified via the actual AI auto-recorder (not just manual click-through): steps 1-8 work exactly as written (Export button, date-range dialog, 'Prepare export' toast, 'Open export' link). Step 9's wait for the export to finish building, however, never completed — the export detail page stayed at '0 items / Not measured yet' for the entire ~45-turn/multi-minute run before the recorder gave up. This matches the same pattern found separately with policy WSP ingestion and account-statement processing: staging appears to lack a registered async-worker deployment for at least some background jobs, so anything depending on one may never finish here even though the trigger/UI side is completely correct. Worth re-testing closer to actual recording time — if it's still stuck, this step may need to be recorded against production instead of staging, or flagged to Hadrius eng as a staging-infra gap.

workflows.title: How to bulk assign tests and categories to an entity
workflows.purpose: Assign multiple compliance test categories, or multiple individual tests, to a client entity in a single action from the Testing program's Entities view.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Entities
In the entities table's toolbar (next to "Add entity"), click "Assign tests/categories" to open the "Assign tests" dialog.
Under "Select client environment", choose the target entity from the dropdown.
On the "Test categories" tab, check the checkbox for each category you want to assign to the entity (each row shows the category name and its test count).

To assign individual tests instead of whole categories, switch to the "Individual saved tests" tab and check the specific tests you want, or use the checkbox in the table header to select all currently filtered tests.
Click "Assign tests" to open the "Confirm and assign" dialog.
Review the client environment and the selected categories or tests shown, then click "Confirm" to assign them to the entity.
prerequisites: At least one client entity already exists under Testing program > Entities (the 'Select client environment' dropdown has nothing to pick otherwise).
The firm's saved-test library already has at least one test category or individual saved test to select (empty library shows 'No categories found' / 'No tests found' and blocks the whole flow).

The target entity has an active compliance manual/policy attached (normally automatic via the company's seeded default policy) — the backend rejects assignment with 'Entity has no active compliance manual' otherwise.

Recording account has Testing program admin permission (FIRM_OVERSIGHT_ADMIN_ACCESS) and the Firm Oversight / Testing program feature is enabled for the tenant — this is an admin-gated, feature-flagged backend action, not available to a read-only persona.

workflows.title: How to correct how a policy's sections were parsed
workflows.purpose: Correct mis-parsed policy headings, hierarchy levels, or split sections using the update sections editor so corrections persist across future document uploads.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies
Locate a policy that already has an uploaded document, and click the row's actions button (three dots icon) on the right
Click "Update sections" in the dropdown menu to open the section hierarchy editor
In the "Update sections" dialog, select the checkbox next to one or more parsed sections that need adjustment, or shift-click a second row to select everything between them
Click "Shift left" to promote the selected section(s) up a hierarchy level, or click "Shift right" to indent them under the section above
Click "Merge up" to combine the selected section(s) into the section directly above them
Alternatively, hover over an individual section row to reveal its inline shift-left, shift-right, and merge icons and use those instead
Use the "Undo" and "Redo" icon buttons in the toolbar to step back and forth through section adjustments if needed
Click "Save corrections" to persist the hierarchy rules and re-apply them to all future uploads of the policy
prerequisites: At least one policy (ComplianceManual) in ACTIVE status that already has a document uploaded (has_content = true) — the "Update sections" menu item is only shown when isCurrent && manual.has_content is true (policy_menu.tsx)
No special role/permission or feature flag is required beyond normal access to Testing program > Policies

The document's parsed sections are derived live from its headings on read (usePolicySections calls a GET .../sections/ endpoint each time, no async parsing job or approval step) — so any policy with an uploaded document has a section tree ready immediately, even if the tree is trivial (a document with no real headings still returns a valid, if flat, tree)
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies

If no row already shows an uploaded document, click a policy's actions button (three dots) and click "Upload document" (or "Upload new version"), then attach a document to it so has_content becomes true and its sections can be parsed
Return to the policy list and click that row's actions button again to reach "Update sections"

Click the "⋮" actions menu button (icon-only, next to the version selector) in the policy header.
Click "Re-analyze" from the dropdown options.

Review the "Re-analyze this policy" dialog: it explains Hadrius will re-read the policy section by section, and once the impact preview loads it lists what will be replaced (counts of tests, scheduled or in-progress runs, risks, and controls).

workflows.title: How to raise a corrective action during test review
workflows.purpose: Flag a questionnaire answer requiring remediation during a test review by assigning an owner, severity level, due date, and instructions before submitting the corrective action.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests
Click the test name in the tests table to open its detail page
Under the "Tests" review view, locate the question response requiring remediation and click "Requires attention"
In the "Requires attention" dialog, select the "Corrective action" option
Select the severity rating in the "Severity level" dropdown
Select the assigned employee in the "Corrective action owner" field
Select the resolution deadline in the "Corrective action due date" picker
Enter detailed remediation instructions in the "Corrective action" text field
Optionally enter supplementary context in "Add note" and attach supporting documentation with "Upload"
Click "Send for corrective action" to submit the corrective action and require resolution before test approval
prerequisites: A test run that is in "Pending review" (or "Pending final review") status — i.e. the test owner has already answered and submitted the questionnaire, and it has not yet been approved or completed

The recording account must itself be an assigned reviewer (first, final, or sole) on that run — admins who are not the assigned reviewer see the review actions locked out (canRecordReviewOutcome / resultsLocked)

At least one question in that run without an outcome already recorded by this reviewer (a question already marked "No objection"/reviewed by this reviewer only reopens via "Change outcome", which this plan's steps don't cover)
At least one active employee to assign as the corrective action owner (Combobox pulls from active employees with firm_oversight.all.basic_access)
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests

If no suitable test exists, click "Create test", complete the wizard, and on the ownership step set both "Add test owner" and "Add test reviewer" to the recording account's own employee (nothing in the code prevents the same person holding both roles) — code comment: "every eligible owner is an eligible reviewer"
Open the test's detail page and click "Start a new test run" (or open an existing DRAFT/IN_PROGRESS run for that test)
Answer every question in the run's questionnaire as the owner
Click "Submit" (the header CTA that calls submitTestRun) to move the run to "Pending review" status

Reload the test run detail page — now that the run is Pending review and the recording account is the assigned reviewer, the per-question "Requires attention" action becomes available for the recorded plan to proceed

workflows.title: How to acknowledge a business risk during test review
workflows.purpose: Accept a flagged issue as a known, acceptable business risk instead of requiring a fix, without blocking approval.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests
Open the test run you are reviewing so its questionnaire loads on the "Tests" tab
Scroll to the flagged question and click "Requires attention" beneath its answer
In the "Requires attention" dialog, select the "Business risk acknowledged" outcome
Select the risk's "Severity level" from the dropdown (optional)
Enter an explanation of why the risk is acceptable in "Add note"
Click "Save & complete" to record the business risk and close the dialog
Confirm the "Business risk acknowledged" outcome badge now appears under the question, and that approval is not blocked

A test run in "Pending review" or "Pending final review" status with the recording account assigned as that run's Reviewer (or sole/Final Reviewer) — this is what makes the per-question "No objection"/"Requires attention" review actions render at all

workflows.title: How to reopen a resolved finding
workflows.purpose: Filter for resolved findings using the status chips, open the finding's side panel, and click the Reopen finding button at the bottom to set it back to Open.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Findings
Click the "Resolved" chip above the findings table to filter to resolved records (this chip only appears when at least one finding is resolved)
Click the row of the resolved finding you want to reopen to open its side panel
Scroll to the bottom of the side panel and click the "Reopen finding" button (it sits to the left of "Save changes", below a border at the bottom of the panel)
Confirm the "Finding reopened" toast appears, and that the status badge near the top of the panel now reads "Open" (it will read "Overdue" instead if the finding's due date has already passed)
Click the X button in the top-right corner of the side panel to close it and return to the findings table
prerequisites: An existing finding whose status is RESOLVED (the "Resolved" chip only renders when resolvedCount > 0, per findings_table.tsx)

Admin permission (Role.Action.FIRM_OVERSIGHT_ADMIN_ACCESS) to add a finding to a test run in the first place, plus FIRM_OVERSIGHT_BASIC_ACCESS with either admin access or finding-owner status to resolve/reopen it (enforced server-side in hadrius_backend firm_oversight/v2/views/findings.py)
At least one existing test run in the Testing program to attach the finding to (findings can only be created from a test run's Findings tab, not from the Findings register page)
At least one active employee to assign as the finding's owner (required field on creation)
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Testing program > Tests and open any existing test
Click into an existing test run for that test
Click the "Findings" tab on the test run detail page
Click the "Add finding" button
Select a "Severity level"
Select a "Finding owner" from the employee list
Pick a "Finding due date"
Fill in the "Finding" field describing the issue
Fill in the "Corrective action" field
Click "Record finding" to submit
Navigate to Testing program > Findings
Click the row of the newly created finding to open its side panel
Click "Mark as resolved" at the bottom of the panel to put it into RESOLVED status
Click the X to close the panel — a resolved finding now exists and the "Resolved" chip will appear for the recorded plan to use

workflows.title: How to schedule a new calendar task
workflows.purpose: Schedule an ad-hoc compliance task on the testing calendar with a title, due date, assignee, and optional recurrence schedule.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Calendar
Click a day cell on the calendar grid to open the day details panel
Click "New Task" in the day details panel header
Enter the task name in the "Title" field
Select a due date using the date picker next to the Title field
Optionally enter task instructions in the "Description" textarea
Click the assignee dropdown and select an employee, or leave it as "Unassigned"
Click the recurrence dropdown and choose a repeat frequency (e.g. "Does not repeat", "Daily", or "Custom...")
If "Custom..." is selected, configure the recurrence interval and end conditions in the "Custom recurrence" dialog that opens
Click "Add Task" to save and schedule the new calendar task

Click on the calendar day cell containing the task you want to modify to open the day details panel on the right
In the day details panel, click on the task row to expand its details
Click "Edit Task" on the expanded task row to open the editing dialog
In the "Edit Task" dialog, update the task name in the "Title" field

Click the "Date" field to select a new due date from the date picker
Click the "Assignee" dropdown and select a new team member to reassign the task

At least one other employee/team member to reassign the task to (beyond whoever it's currently assigned to)

Click "New Task" in the day details panel
Type a title (e.g. "Demo task") into the "Title" field

workflows.title: How to cancel or delete a calendar task
workflows.purpose: Delete a one-time calendar task or choose whether to cancel a single occurrence or the entire series for a recurring task.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Calendar
Click on the calendar day cell containing the task you want to cancel or delete to open the day details panel
In the day details panel, click on the task row to expand its details and actions
Click "Delete" on the expanded task card
For a one-time task with no recurrence, the task is immediately removed without an extra confirmation dialog
For a recurring task, review the options presented in the "Confirm Cancellation" dialog
Click "This Instance Only" to cancel only the selected occurrence of the recurring task
Alternatively, click "Entire Series" to delete all scheduled occurrences of the task
Alternatively, click "Nevermind" to close the confirmation dialog without making changes

At least one recurring calendar task exists (created with a repeat cadence such as Weekly/Daily), to demonstrate the "Confirm Cancellation" dialog with This Instance Only / Entire Series options
Standard Testing program access (firm_oversight.all.basic_access), which any account using this module already has

Click on a calendar day cell to open the day details panel
Click "New Task" in the day details panel
Type a title (e.g. "Demo one-time task") in the title field
Leave the recurrence dropdown on "Does not repeat"

Click on a calendar day cell again (same or different day) to open the day details panel

workflows.title: How to send continuing education reminder emails
workflows.purpose: Send default or custom reminder emails to employees with incomplete or overdue continuing education course assignments, from the Courses view of the Continuing education tab.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Continuing education
Click the "Courses" tab (the page opens on the "Employees" tab by default; the course-level reminder actions only appear on the Courses tab).

Locate the target course in the Courses table. Either check the row's checkbox (and any other courses' checkboxes) to reveal the bulk action bar and click "Send reminders", or open the row's actions menu (three dots) and select "Send reminder" to target only that course. ("Send reminder" is disabled when the course has no enrolled employees or no incomplete assignments.)

In the "Choose an Email Template" dialog that opens, review the recipient count shown as "Sending to N employees" (or "Sending to 1 employee") — this reflects the employees with incomplete (not-yet-completed) assignments for the course(s) you selected.

Confirm the success toast titled "Success" appears, with a description such as "Reminders sent for 1 course" (wording varies with the number of courses and whether a default or custom template was sent), confirming the reminder emails were dispatched.

The 'Continuing education' / WebCE module enabled for the company (confirmed active for this tenant)

workflows.title: How to notify an employee about an expired account connection
workflows.purpose: Send an email reminder prompting an employee to reconnect an expired or disconnected brokerage account from their profile.
steps: Navigate to People directory in the left sidebar.
Click on an employee row in the People directory table to open their profile.
Click the "Accounts" tab on the employee's profile.
In the connections table, locate a connection whose "Connection status" column shows a "Connection expired" badge.
Click the "Actions" button above the connections table, then click "Send email reminder" in the dropdown menu.

In the "Send reminder email?" dialog, review the description ("Send an email reminding this employee to connect or reconnect their investment accounts.") and click "Send". A confirmation toast reading "Email sent" appears once it succeeds.
prerequisites: At least one employee brokerage connection whose Connection status is 'Connection expired' (backend status BROKEN) — as of a live check just now, company 1013 has 0 connections in BROKEN status (5 GOOD, 10 MISSING_LETTER, 35 MISSING_STATEMENTS), so this state does not currently exist for the demo tenant.

Viewing the employee's Accounts tab as an admin/compliance user, not as that employee's own self-view — the 'Send email reminder' button (component_fix_connections_email_button.tsx) calls showEmployeeAccountView() and renders null in the employee's own view.
workflows.blockerReason: A connection's 'Connection expired' badge (frontend: getConnectionAttentionType() mapping external_connection_status === 'BROKEN' -> NEEDS_REPAIR, in apps/hadrius-app/src/pages/employees/connections/brokerage_account_utilities.ts) is driven entirely by EmployeeBrokerConnection.external_connection_status = BROKEN on the backend. Searching hadrius_backend shows BROKEN is only ever set by (1) external sync/reconciliation jobs — snaptrade/service_snaptrade.py (remote_connection_status from the SnapTrade API), meld/sync_meld_connection_status.py (hadrius_connection.external_connection_status = BROKEN based on Meld's reported state), and Plaid webhook/reconciliation paths — or (2) derive_connection_status_from_accounts() in connections/service_update_account_status.py, which itself only turns BROKEN when an underlying EmployeeAccount.status is BROKEN, again a value only written by those same external sync services. There is no admin/user-facing API view or UI control anywhere in hadrius_frontend or hadrius_backend that lets an operator directly set a connection or account to BROKEN — the only backend endpoints touching broken connections (views_employees.py, views_trade_monitoring_employees.py, views_trade_monitoring_connections.py) all just read/count/filter on the existing status. Producing a 'Connection expired' row therefore requires an actual real-world disconnection/revocation on the linked broker's side (Plaid, SnapTrade, or Meld sandbox), which is external-system-dependent and outside the Hadrius app UI. A live query against the staging DB (company_id=1013) confirms zero BROKEN connections currently exist there (statuses present: GOOD=5, MISSING_LETTER=10, MISSING_STATEMENTS=35), so there is nothing to click on for this step today.

workflows.title: How an employee completes and signs a certification
workflows.purpose: An employee opens an assigned certification task from their own Certifications page, answers all required questions, reviews the Final disclaimer attestation, and submits the certification (with their prefilled identity confirmed) for compliance review.
steps: Navigate to the Certifications tab in the employee self-service portal sidebar (this is the employee's own view — a separate persona/route tree from the People oversight admin module, which does not host this flow).

On the Certifications page, click on an assigned certification that still needs action (status "Not started" or "Draft"; use the "Waiting" filter pill to find outstanding ones) to open the questionnaire.
Review the template description and due date shown in the header, then answer each question — for example, select "Yes" or "No" for a yes/no question.

If a question includes a follow-up text question or a document-upload question, type your answer or drag files into the upload area (up to 10 files, each under 50 MB) to attach supporting documentation.
Click "Next" to advance through each question until you reach the "Final disclaimer" section at the end of the questionnaire.
Review the two attestation statements defined by the certification template and check both boxes to confirm agreement.
Confirm the prefilled legal first name, last name, email, and date shown in the Final disclaimer card — these are read-only fields populated from your profile, not typed entry.
Click "Submit" (shown as "Resubmit" if the certification was returned for revision) to submit the certification for compliance review.
prerequisites: An employee with a certification task in "Not started", "Draft", or "Action required" status (i.e. assigned but not yet submitted) — confirmed live via DB query: company 1013 currently has ~18 CertTask rows with status IN_PROGRESS/review_status UNREVIEWED across distinct employees, from an active quarterly (Q2 2026 capture period) recurring certification round, due 2026-09-24.

A way to view the /employee/certifications self-service portal as that employee: either direct employee-role login credentials, or an admin account with impersonation rights (the frontend has a built-in impersonation_selector / onBehalfOf mechanism, so a demo admin account likely does not need separate employee credentials).

The assigned certification's template should include a mix of question types (at least one yes/no, and ideally one follow-up-text or document-upload question) plus the standard Final disclaimer section with two attestation checkboxes, so every step in the plan has something to click — verify the specific task picked for recording actually has these before rehearsing.
The target employee's profile should have legal first/last name and email populated so the Final disclaimer's prefilled identity fields aren't blank (standard for any onboarded employee record).
suggestedSetupSteps: Log in with the demo admin account and open the People oversight > Certifications module to confirm at least one active round exists for company 1013.

Use impersonation (or an employee-role login) to open /employee/certifications for one specific employee, click the "Waiting" filter pill, and confirm at least one task shows "Not started" or "Draft".

Open that task and click through its questions once before recording to confirm it contains a yes/no question, a follow-up text or document-upload question, and the Final disclaimer section with two attestation checkboxes — if the first task picked lacks variety, pick a different employee/task from the Waiting list that does.

workflows.title: How to review and approve or reject a disclosure
workflows.purpose: Review assigned disclosure submissions from the Approvals queue, inspect the employee's submitted responses and any flagged answers, and approve, reject, or send the disclosure back to the employee for corrections.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Disclosures.

On the Disclosures dashboard's "Approvals" tab (the default view), click "Start review" to open the first item in your assigned review queue, or click the arrow-icon "View disclosure" button on any pending row to open that submission's review pane directly.
In the review pane, review the employee's submitted responses and any flagged answers; use the "⋮ More actions" menu's "Download submission" item to view or export uploaded documentation.
To leave an internal note, open the activity panel on the right side of the review pane, switch to the "Comments" view, and type your note in the "Add a comment..." field.
To approve the disclosure, click "Approve." If there are unreviewed flagged responses, an "Approve with unreviewed flags" dialog appears — click "Approve anyway" to confirm.

To reject the disclosure instead, open the "⋮ More actions" menu and click "Reject disclosure." In the "Reject disclosure" dialog, optionally enter a note in the "Reason (optional)" field, then click "Reject disclosure" to confirm.

To send the disclosure back to the employee for corrections instead, click "Send back" (enabled once the disclosure is submitted and, if it has question responses, at least one has been marked non-compliant). In the "Send back for update" dialog, enter at least 10 characters in the "Reason for sending back" field, then click "Send back" to confirm.
prerequisites: Reviewer permission that makes the recording account an eligible approver (isEligibleApprover) for at least one disclosure — otherwise Approve/Reject/Send back render disabled with 'Only assigned approvers can take action.'

At least one disclosure submission in Pending review status assigned to the recording account, so the Approvals tab's 'Start review' button is enabled (it is hard-disabled — disabled={myReviewIds.length === 0} — when the reviewer's queue is empty) and at least one arrow-icon 'View disclosure' row exists to click directly

That pending disclosure should have actual question responses (not just a 'nothing to disclose' submission) so there is something to mark compliant/non-compliant and to demonstrate 'Send back' — Send back only enables once at least one response is marked NON_COMPLIANT (canSendBack = isEligibleApprover && isSubmitted && (!hasResponses || hasNonCompliant)), which the reviewer can set live in the review pane via the compliance toggle on a response

Optional, not required for the core flow: a pending disclosure with auto-flagged responses to show the 'Approve with unreviewed flags' dialog branch — flag_count is system/rule-generated from the employee's actual answers, not something the reviewer sets manually
Permission to use 'Assign disclosures' > 'Log on behalf' (ASSIGN_DISCLOSURES_PERMISSION / canSubmitOnBehalf) as a fallback path if the Approvals queue is ever empty at recording time
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to People oversight > Disclosures > Approvals tab and check whether the 'Start review' button shows a nonzero count; if it does, and at least one row is visible, no setup is needed.
If the queue is empty (or you want a guaranteed fresh item), click 'Assign disclosures'.
In the Assign disclosures wizard, on the recipients step, select an employee (yourself or a convenient test employee) as the recipient.
On the templates step, select a disclosure template that has real questions (e.g. a Gifts & Entertainment or Outside Business Activities template), not a document-only one.
On the reviewers step, add yourself (the recording account) as a reviewer so the resulting disclosure lands in your own Approvals queue.
On the summary step, click the dropdown arrow next to 'Assign disclosures' and choose 'Log on behalf' ('Create these for you to fill; employees aren't emailed.').

In the fill-on-behalf modal that opens, answer the questionnaire — choosing an answer likely to trigger a flag on at least one question if you want to demo the flagged-response path — then click Submit to submit it as the employee's response.

Confirm the new disclosure now appears in People oversight > Disclosures > Approvals with status 'Pending review' and is assigned to you, so 'Start review' / the arrow 'View disclosure' button are enabled.

workflows.title: How to review and approve an employee's certification submission
workflows.purpose: Review an employee's submitted certification responses, evaluate auto-flagged answers, optionally mark individual responses as compliant or non-compliant with a note, and approve the submission.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > Certifications.
Click the "Submissions" tab to display the table of all employee certification submissions across every campaign.

Click the "Needs review" filter pill (or open the filter panel and use its "Status" section) to narrow the list to submissions awaiting review, then click on the target employee's submission row (or the arrow button in that row's Actions column) to open the task detail page.

Inspect the submitted answers. Any response that was automatically flagged shows a red flag badge with the specific reason it was flagged; the "Flags" column back on the submissions list also shows each submission's total flag count.
Review any attached disclosure documents, attestation acknowledgements, or uploaded files, which appear inline beneath their corresponding question.

Optional: beneath any individual response, click "Compliant" or "Non-compliant". prerequisites: Access to People oversight > Check Blotter, which is gated behind the employee_c8e feature flag plus module permission (page_people_oversight_upsell.tsx shows an upsell/no-access state when either is missing) — expected to already be enabled for the Hadrius demo tenant but worth a quick check before recording

workflows.title: How to file a new Form U5
workflows.purpose: Initiate, complete, sign, and submit a Form U5 termination filing to FINRA for an employee leaving the firm.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > U5 filings.
Click "File New U5" to start a new Form U5 filing; this opens the multi-step filing wizard at /finra/u5/new.
On the "Preliminary information" step, use "Select employee" to choose the representative being terminated, confirm the filing firm in "Select firm", and click "Next: General information".
On the "General information" step, review personal details, verify or update fields in "Section 3: Current residential address", and click "Next: Termination information".

On the "Termination information" step, under "Section 1: Termination details" select Yes or No for "Is this a full termination?", choose a "Reason for termination", pick the "Date terminated (MM/DD/YYYY)", and click "Next: Disclosures".
On the "Disclosures" step, answer the questions under each disclosure category or click "Answer \"No\" to all" for a section, then click "Next: Disclosure reporting pages".
On the "Disclosure reporting pages" step, review the disclosure reporting pages message and click "Next: Review".
On the "Review" step, review all filing information and click "Save and proceed to signatures" to create the filing record.

On the resulting "Edit Form U5 filing" page's Signatures step, under "Firm acknowledgment" enter the contact person, telephone number, and signatory name, check the acknowledgment checkbox, and click "Sign firm acknowledgment"; if an "Individual acknowledgment and consent" section is also shown, enter the printed name, check its checkbox, and click "Sign individual acknowledgment".
Click "Back to filing" to open the filing detail page for this employee's U5.
Click "Validate filing" to run FINRA validation, then once the filing is ready click "File U5 to FINRA" and confirm by clicking "Submit filing" in the "Submit U5 filing" dialog.
prerequisites: A registered employee who is ACTIVE, has a CRD number, has an initial U4 filing on record, and does not already have a U5 filing (only such employees appear in the "Select employee" picker)
That employee must have a current (non-terminated) PRIMARY firm association, so a filing firm auto-populates or can be chosen in "Select firm"

The filing firm must already have valid, real FINRA API credentials (client_id/secret) connected under Firm profile > FINRA API credentials — 'Validate filing' and 'File U5 to FINRA' call FINRA's live production filing API (api.finra.org) even for this internal sandbox company, not a safe mock, so this cannot be faked with placeholder values entered in the credentials UI
workflows.blockerReason: In hadrius_backend, finra_client.py sets is_qa only for QA_COMPANY_IDS=[1,435,501] (company 1013 "Stephen Investments" is not in that list). Because 1013 is a sandbox (INTERNAL_COMPANY_IDS in data_ops/management/commands/set_sandbox_company_types.py), it gets call_mock=True but is_qa=False, so FinraClient.BASE_URL resolves to "https://api.finra.org" (FINRA's live production API) in finra_client_impl.py. The methods actually invoked by "Validate filing" and "File U5 to FINRA" — validate_u5_filing_with_operations and submit_u5_filing_specific — always hit self.BASE_URL regardless of call_mock (call_mock only swaps the URL for a couple of unrelated read-only lookups like get_composite_individual_data). get_finra_access_token_for_firm (finra/service.py) also requires a real FinraAPICredentials row and calls FINRA's real OAuth host to get a token. There is no demo/internal-company bypass in finra/jobs/submit_u5.py — any failure just marks the filing FAILED. This means the last two plan steps need a real, working FINRA production credential for the filing firm that cannot be created through the app's own UI (the credentials form only stores what you type; FINRA must actually accept it), and if such a credential is already wired up, actually completing the step files a real, live termination with FINRA — not a safe demo action either way.
suggestedSetupSteps: Before recording, confirm with Hadrius engineering/ops whether the filing firm on company 1013 already has a working FINRA API credential (Firm profile > FINRA API credentials) and, if so, whether it points at a real vs. throwaway FINRA relationship

If credentials are missing or unverified, plan to stop the recording after "Validate filing" fails (or before clicking it) rather than attempting "File U5 to FINRA" / "Submit filing", to avoid either a stuck recording or a real regulatory submission

workflows.title: How to file a Form U4 amendment
workflows.purpose: Initiate and submit a Form U4 amendment filing for a representative to update registration information.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > U4 filings
Click "File New U4" to open the "Create new Form U4 filing" dialog
Select the "Amendment" option and click "Continue" to open the filing wizard
Under "Section 1: Select representative", search for the representative in "Search for a representative's name or email" and click their name from the results
Under "Section 2: Select amendment type", choose the desired amendment category (e.g. "State registration")
Click "Next: Enter amendment details" to advance to the "Enter details" step
Complete the required fields for the selected amendment type on the "Enter details" step, then click "Next: Review & submit"
Review the amendment details on the "Review & submit" step and click "Continue to signatures" to save the amendment and proceed to signatures
prerequisites: Admin role on the recording account — creating a U4 amendment is admin-gated on the backend (`@has_role_access(User.Role.ADMIN)` on the create/update endpoints), even though the 'File New U4' button itself isn't visibly restricted in the UI.

The FINRA/U4 module enabled for the tenant (`finra_api_enabled` feature flag backs `@feature_enabled(FINRA)` on the amendment endpoints and the whole People oversight > U4 filings route) — very likely already on for this tenant since it's Hadrius's internal FINRA/broker-dealer demo company and the route was confirmed to render in the prior verification pass.

At least one ACTIVE employee who is a real FINRA-registered representative: has a CRD number set AND already has an underlying FirmAssociation record (finra_profile not null). The frontend representative picker only filters on `status === 'ACTIVE' && crd_number` — it does NOT check for a firm association — but the backend create endpoint (`post_create_u4_amendment`) hard-rejects with 400 'finra/amendment/no_firm_association' if the selected employee lacks one. If 'State registration' or 'SRO registration' amendment type is used (as in the plan's example), no pre-existing registration data is actually required — the form lets the operator fill values from scratch — so this is not an extra precondition.

Click the employee actions menu and choose "Connect to FINRA" (or "Sync from FINRA").

Enter the representative's CRD number and date of birth, then submit — this tenant's FINRA integration is mocked (company 1013 is classified INTERNAL/sandbox, so `finra_client()` always uses `call_mock=True`), so the sync succeeds immediately without any real external FINRA connectivity and creates the underlying FirmAssociation record needed for amendments.

Confirm the sync completed (toast says "Sync successful" / "Account connected and synced"), then return to People oversight > U4 filings and use this employee as the representative in Section 1 of the amendment wizard.

workflows.title: How to file a new Form U5 for a departing representative

Review the prefilled "General information" step and click "Next: Termination information"
On "Termination information" under "Section 1: Termination details", answer "Is this a full termination?" with the Yes/No radio

Select a "Reason for termination:" radio ("Deceased", "Discharged", "Other", "Permitted to resign", or "Voluntary"); if you chose Discharged, Permitted to resign, or Other, fill in the required "Termination explanation:" textarea
Pick the termination date with the "Select termination date" date picker, then click "Next: Disclosures"
Answer the "Disclosures" questions and click "Next: Disclosure reporting pages"; complete any required DRPs and click "Next: Review"
On "Review", click "Save and proceed to signatures"; a "U5 filing created" toast appears and the stepper moves to "Signatures"

In the "Submit U5 filing" dialog, click "Submit filing"

To delete: click "Delete [N]"; the "Bulk Delete Filings" dialog lists "The following N filings will be permanently deleted:"

workflows.title: How to bulk sign, validate, and submit U4 filings

Click "Sign [N]"; the "Bulk Sign Filings" dialog opens
Under "Signature Details", leave the prefilled "Date" and type your name in "15E Signatory Name" (placeholder "Enter your name")
Review the list under "The following N filings will be signed:" and click "Sign N filings"
Watch "Progress: X/N completed"; if any row shows "Failed", click "Retry N failed filings"

Click "Validate N filings" and wait for "Progress: X/N completed" (rows that fail show "Validation failed"; fix them via "View" and click "Retry N failed filings")

Click "Close" to return to the directory

Selected U4 filings that are missing their individual and/or firm signature ("Sign [N]" is disabled if all are already signed) and are Unvalidated / Failed validation for the validate step

steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Settings" in the "Marketing Projects" page header (opens /marketing/settings, page title "Settings")
Click the "Expiration dates" tab
In the "Expiration by document type" card, click "Add document type override" (shown in the "No document type overrides" empty state, or at the top-right of the card once overrides exist)
In the "Add document type override" dialog, open the "Document type" combobox (placeholder "Select a type", search box "Search document types...") and pick a document type
In "Expires after", type a number and pick the unit ("Days", "Months" or "Years") from the adjoining dropdown
Click "Add override". The dialog closes and a row appears in the table with columns "Document type", "Expiration", "Auto-renew", "Auto-resubmit", "Actions"
Optionally toggle "Auto-renew" or "Auto-resubmit" on the new row
Click "Save changes" in the page header. A "Settings saved." toast appears
prerequisites: Marketing Review module enabled for the company
Access to Marketing settings (the page is reached via the "Settings" button on the Marketing Projects page or dashboards; it is not in the sidebar)
At least one document type exists in the firm's document type library (defaults are present); a type already overridden is hidden from the combobox

workflows.title: How to reject a marketing document with a reason
workflows.purpose: From the Approver Dashboard, claim an unclaimed marketing document in your review tier and reject it with an explanatory note that is returned to the submitter.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Dashboard" in the "Marketing Projects" page header (opens /marketing/dashboard - the "Approver" "Dashboard")
Stay on the "Overview" tab (other tabs: "Projects & Documents", "Activity")
In the "N unclaimed in my tier" table, click "Claim" on the document's row

In the "Claim review" dialog ("You'll become the active reviewer for \"<document>\". Others in your tier will see you've claimed it."), click "Claim review". A "Success" toast reads "\"<document>\" claimed." and the document moves to the "N documents assigned to me" table
In the assigned document's row, click the reject icon button (aria-label "Reject", tooltip "Reject document") next to the "Review" button

In the "Reject document" dialog ("\"<document>\" will be returned to the submitter for revision."), type the explanation in "Reason for rejection (optional)" (placeholder "Let the submitter know what needs changing...")
Click "Reject document". A "Success" toast reads "\"<document>\" rejected." and the row leaves your assigned table
prerequisites: Marketing Review module enabled and marketing config enable_dashboards = true (otherwise the "Dashboard" header button is hidden; /marketing/dashboard is still a valid URL)
User has an exact approver permission (marketing_review.documents.approver.write_all or .write_scoped) - the route shows "Approver dashboard" no-permissions view otherwise
User belongs to an approval group in the current approval step of at least one submitted, unclaimed document (so it appears in "unclaimed in my tier" with can_claim)
The claimed document must be approvable by this user (can_approve) for the Reject button to be enabled
suggestedSetupSteps: Create workflow groups (Marketing > Workflows > "Groups" > "Create group") and put the recording user in an approver group
Create and activate an approval workflow whose approval step uses that group (see "How to create a new approval workflow")
As a submitter in the workflow's submitter group, create a project and upload a document through Marketing > Projects (see "How to create a new marketing project") so it lands in the approver's tier

workflows.title: How to export marketing review data
workflows.purpose: Filter marketing projects and documents on the Exports page, choose the columns to include, and download the data as a CSV or a ZIP export (or export the disclosure library as CSV).
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Exports (page title "Exports")
Stay on the "Projects & documents" tab (the other tab is "Disclosures")

In the "Filters" accordion, optionally set a "Date range" with "Start date" / "End date", and narrow by "Audience", "Document category", "Review status", "Workflow", "Submitter group", "Filter by submitter" or "Filter by approver"
Expand the "Fields to include" accordion and check or uncheck the columns for the export ("Reset to defaults" restores the default set; at least one field must be selected)
Review the "Preview" section showing the matching documents
Click "Download CSV export" in the page header to download the CSV directly

Or click "Download ZIP export": a "Generating export…" toast appears, then "Export ready. Downloading…" once the ZIP is built; the job is listed in "Export history" below where it can be downloaded again
Optionally switch to the "Disclosures" tab, set "Status", "Tags", "Rules" or date filters, and click "Export disclosures (CSV)"
prerequisites: Marketing Review module enabled for the company (sidebar "Exports" child under "Marketing")
At least one marketing project with documents so the preview and export contain rows (page works, but exports would be empty otherwise)
suggestedSetupSteps: If no projects exist, create one via Marketing > Projects (see "How to create a new marketing project")

workflows.title: How to create a new disclosure in Marketing
workflows.purpose: Create a new disclosure in the Marketing disclosure library with a title, disclosure copy, optional tags, usage instructions and linked rules, and activate it.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Disclosures
On the "Disclosures" tab, click "New disclosure" (top-right of the table). The "New disclosure" page opens
Enter the name in "Title" (placeholder "Enter disclosure name"); optionally fill "External identifier"
In the "Disclosure" section, type the required wording into the "Disclosure copy" textarea; toggle "Preview disclosure" to see it rendered
Optionally click "Add tags" and select tags in the dialog; chosen tags appear as badges
Optionally enter guidance in "Use instructions (optional)"
Optionally click "Insert Rules" to link existing disclosure rules; they appear under "Selected Rules (N)"
Click "Save & activate" (or "Save as draft"). A "Success" toast reads "Disclosure created and activated successfully" and you return to the disclosures table where the new row shows status "Active"
prerequisites: Marketing Review module enabled for the company
User has permission marketing_review.disclosures.write_all (otherwise "New disclosure" is disabled with tooltip "You don't have permission to create or edit disclosures.")

workflows.title: How to create a new approval workflow
workflows.purpose: Build a multi-step marketing approval workflow by assigning a submitter group and approver groups in the drag-and-drop builder, then name and activate it.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Workflows
On the "Workflows" tab, click "Create workflow" (next to the "Search workflows" box). The "Create approval workflow" page opens on the "Build & preview" step
In "Drag & drop workflow builder", under "Workflow groups" (search box "Find a group"), drag a group card onto the "Submitter" drop zone labelled "Drop here"
Drag one or more group cards onto the "Step 1" "Approvers" drop zone; when a step has several groups, click "All groups must approve" to toggle whether every group or any one group must approve
Optionally click the round "Add approver(s)" area to add "Step 2" and drop more groups into it
Check the "Workflow preview (N approval steps)" section ending in "Final approval", then click "Continue"
On the "Automate & activate" step, enter the "Workflow name" (placeholder "Enter workflow name") and optionally "Workflow description"
Optionally turn on "Set as default workflow" and adjust the default flags and notification settings
Click "Activate workflow" (or "Save as draft"). A "Success" toast reads "Workflow created and activated successfully" and you return to /marketing/workflows where the workflow is listed
prerequisites: Marketing Review module enabled for the company

At least two workflow groups exist (one to use as submitter, one as approver); the builder shows "No groups available" otherwise and "Continue" stays disabled until a submitter and at least one approver group are placed
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Marketing > Workflows, click the "Groups" tab and click "Create group" (/marketing/workflows/groups/new) to create a submitter group and an approver group with members

workflows.title: How to create a disclosure rule to auto-attach disclosures
workflows.purpose: Create a rule-based disclosure rule that, when a document matches conditions such as its document category, requires the selected disclosures on that document.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Disclosures
Click the "Rules" tab
Click "Add New Rule" (next to the search box "Search by rule name, trigger type, or Admin name"). The "Add rule" page opens ("Define a condition when a disclosure should be applied to a document.")
Under "Automation type", select "Rule-based" (other options: "AI-suggested", "Non-automated")
Enter a name in "Rule name" and optionally a "Description"

Under "Rule-Based Conditions", either switch on "Apply to all documents" or configure the condition row: leave "Apply when", choose a field (for example "Document category"), an operator, and a value ("Select value" lists document types); click "Add Condition" for more AND/OR rows
Click "Find disclosures". The "Disclosure Suggestions" step lists disclosures (search with "Find a disclosure")
Click "Accept" on each disclosure the rule should attach; the "Total" line updates. Click "Next"
On the confirm step, review the accepted disclosures table and click "Create rule". A "Success" toast reads "Rule \"<name>\" created successfully" and you return to the rules table
prerequisites: Marketing Review module enabled for the company
User has permission marketing_review.disclosures.write_all (otherwise "Add New Rule" is disabled)
At least one active disclosure exists to accept on the "Disclosure Suggestions" step
Document types exist in the firm library (used as values for the "Document category" condition)
suggestedSetupSteps: Navigate to Marketing > Disclosures, click "New disclosure", fill "Title" and "Disclosure copy", click "Save & activate"

workflows.title: How to create a new marketing project
workflows.purpose: A submitter starts a new marketing review project from the Marketing Projects board, walks the three-step wizard (Set up project, Upload, Save project), attaches at least one document, picks or is routed to an approval workflow, completes document details, and creates the project.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects (the "Marketing Projects" board).

Click "New" in the filter bar under the page header to open the project creation wizard at /marketing/project/new; the header shows the title "Untitled project" with a "Draft" badge and the tabs "Set up project", "Upload", "Save project".
On the "Project details" sub-step (left stepper), type a name in the "Project name" field (required) and optionally a description in the "Overview" textarea.
Click "Next" to move to the "Add documents" sub-step.

Drag a file into the dropzone (guidance text reads "Upload up to N files, up to X each (Y total)") or click it to pick a file; the document appears in the list below. Alternatively click "Open document builder" to author a document in the "Document builder" dialog.

Click "Next" to move to "Workflow setup" (labelled "Routing questions" when the company uses a routing questionnaire). If more than one workflow is available, select the approval workflow; with a single workflow it is pre-selected. In the routing-questionnaire variant, answer the required questions instead.

Click "Next" to move to "Submission questions"; expand each document accordion and complete its document details (document type, dates, review flags and any configured submission questions). Items still missing show a "Needs your attention" badge.
Click "Save documents" (the Next button's label on this sub-step) to advance to the "Upload" step; each document shows an upload progress card ending in "Upload completed!".

Click "Next" to reach the "Save project" step, which shows "Project summary review" with the project, submitter, description, "Flags applied:" and "Workflow preview:" sections plus the documents table.
Click "Create project" in the page header to submit. ("Save as draft" saves progress and returns to the submitter dashboard; "Cancel" discards the draft.)
prerequisites: Company has the marketing_review feature and the user has marketing access (ModuleAccessView gating).
At least one active approval workflow whose submitter group includes the user (the wizard blocks with "Select a workflow" otherwise), or an active routing questionnaire.
A sample file to upload (accepted marketing document types, e.g. a PDF).
suggestedSetupSteps: If no workflow exists: Marketing > Workflows > create a workflow whose submitter group includes the recording user (see the 'How to create a new approval workflow' plan).

workflows.title: How to configure document expiration and renewal rules
workflows.purpose: Turn on firm-wide expiration for approved marketing documents, set default durations and near-expiration windows, choose auto-renew or auto-resubmit behavior, add a per-document-type override, and configure who is notified when documents approach or pass expiration.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Settings" in the page header (opens /marketing/settings).
Click the "Expiration dates" tab.
In the "Firm-wide expiration" card, turn on the switch (aria-label "Firm-wide expiration"); the card's fields become editable.
Under "Default document expiration", enter a value and unit in "Default expiration".
Optionally set the "Near-expiration badge" and "Near-expiration notification" windows.
Under "When an approval expires", toggle either "Renew it automatically" or "Resubmit it for a new approval" (both off means the approval simply lapses).
If "Resubmit it for a new approval" is on, fill the "Resubmit [N] days [before/after] the expiration date." row with a day count and timing.
In the "Expiration by document type" card, click "Add document type override".

In the "Add document type override" dialog, pick a type in the "Document type" combobox and set "Expires after", then click "Add override"; a row appears in the table with "Expiration", "Auto-renew" and "Auto-resubmit" columns.
Optionally toggle the row's "Auto-renew" or "Auto-resubmit" switch.
In the "Per-document overrides" card, toggle the switch to let document owners turn auto-resubmit on or off for their own documents.
In the "Expiration notifications" card, turn on "Enable", then tick the "Admin", "Approver" and/or "Submitter" checkboxes for the "Expiration approaching" and "Document expired" rows.
Click "Save changes" in the page header; a "Settings saved." toast confirms.

workflows.title: How to claim and approve a marketing document
workflows.purpose: From the Approver Dashboard, claim an unclaimed document in your tier so you become its active reviewer, then approve it (optionally with a note) so it advances to the next workflow step or receives final approval.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Dashboard" in the page header (only shown when dashboards are enabled) to open the "Approver Dashboard" at /marketing/dashboard on its "Overview" tab.
In the "N unclaimed in my tier" table, find the document and click "Claim" on its row ("Claim this page" claims every claimable row at once).
In the "Claim review" dialog, click "Claim review"; a "Success" toast reads "\"<document>\" claimed." and the document moves to the "N documents assigned to me" table.
Optionally click "Review" on the assigned row to open the document review page and inspect the document, then return to the dashboard.
On the assigned row, click the Approve icon button (tooltip "Approve document").
In the "Approve document" dialog, optionally enter text in "Approval note (optional)" (a comment template can be picked), and note the "Final approval" or "Next step: ..." badge.
Click "Approve document"; a "Success" toast reads "\"<document>\" approved." and the row leaves your assigned list.
prerequisites: Marketing review config has enable_dashboards = true (otherwise /marketing/dashboard redirects to /marketing/projects).
The user is a marketing approver (useIsMarketingApproverExact) and a member of an approval group on the document's current workflow step.
At least one submitted document sitting at an approver step that nobody has claimed yet.
suggestedSetupSteps: Ask an admin to enable dashboards in the marketing review config if the "Dashboard" button is not visible on Marketing Projects.

Create a project with one document via Marketing > Projects > "New" using a workflow whose first approval step includes the recording user's approval group; wait for AI processing to finish so it lands in the approver queue.

workflows.title: How to configure project submission questions
workflows.purpose: Choose how often submitters answer document details and submission questions, then build the custom questionnaire (with question types, options, required flags and conditional display) that submitters complete when creating a marketing review project.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Settings" in the page header.
Click the "Submission questions" tab.

In the "How submitters answer" card, choose a radio option: "Let the submitter choose", "Once per project" or "Once per document"; it saves immediately with a "Submission questions scope saved." toast.
Click "Create questionnaire" in the "No submission questions yet" empty state (or "Edit" next to the "Submission questions" heading if a questionnaire already exists).
Click "Add question" to append a "Question 1" card.
Type the prompt in "Question label" and pick a "Question type" ("Date", "Single select", "Multi select" or "Long text"); optionally fill "Placeholder (optional)" and "Tooltip (optional)".
For "Single select" or "Multi select", fill the "Value" field under "Answer options" and click "Add option" for more choices.
Toggle "Required" in the card header to make the answer mandatory.
For a second or later question, toggle "Conditional" and use the "Trigger question", "Operator" and "Value" fields (click "Add condition" for additional rules).
Click "Save questionnaire"; a "Submission questions saved." toast confirms and the editor returns to read-only mode.
prerequisites: Company marketing_review status is ACTIVE and the user holds the exact permission marketing_review.workflows.write_all (the tab is hidden otherwise).

workflows.title: How to add a new document to an existing marketing project
workflows.purpose: Open an existing marketing project's details page and add one or more new documents to it through the "+ New document" flow, setting document type, dates and review flags before upload.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects.
Click a project card on the board to open its "Project details page" (/marketing/project/<id>/).
In the documents workflow-progress section, click "+ New document" (disabled with the tooltip "Workflow is not active" if the project's workflow is inactive).
In the "Add documents to project" dialog, drop or choose the file(s), then click "Continue".

In the "Document details" dialog ("Set up N document(s)"), pick a "Document type" from the combobox, choose a "Due date" and optionally "Date of use (optional)", answer any submission questions, and select review flags if the workflow does not fix them.
Click "Apply Settings & Add" (or "Add with Defaults" when saved defaults exist); files upload and a "Success" toast reads "N document(s) added successfully".
Confirm the new document row appears in the project's documents table with its initial status.
prerequisites: At least one existing marketing project on the board whose workflow is active.
The user can submit to that project (project submitter/collaborator or has change_submitter permission).
A sample file to upload (e.g. a PDF).
suggestedSetupSteps: Create a project first via Marketing > Projects > "New" if the board is empty.

workflows.title: How to configure comment templates for document review
workflows.purpose: Create, edit and delete reusable comment templates that approvers can pick when writing approval, rejection or review notes on marketing documents.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Settings" in the page header.
Click the "Comment templates" tab.
Click "Add template" (in the card header, or in the "No comment templates yet" empty state).
In the "Add template" dialog, enter a "Title" and the reusable text in "Body".
Click "Save"; the template appears as a row in the table with "Title", "Body" and "Actions" columns.
Optionally click the pencil icon (aria-label "Edit <title>") to open the "Edit template" dialog, change the fields and click "Save".
Optionally click the trash icon (aria-label "Delete <title>") to remove a template from the list.
Click "Save changes" in the page header; a "Settings saved." toast confirms.
prerequisites: Company has the marketing_review feature and the user can reach Marketing settings.

workflows.title: How to configure marketing document types
workflows.purpose: Manage the firm's marketing document type library: add custom types, toggle which types are active for submitters, rename or delete custom types, and save the library.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Settings" in the page header.
Click the "Document types" tab.
Click "Add document type" in the section header.
In the "Add document type" dialog, type a name in the "Document type" field and click "Add type"; the new row shows a "Custom" badge and is active.
Toggle the switch in the "Active" column of any row to enable or disable that type for submissions.
On a custom type's row, open the actions menu (aria-label "<name> actions") and choose "Edit"; in the "Edit document type" dialog change the name and click "Save changes".
For an unused custom type, open the actions menu and choose "Delete", then click "Delete type" in the "Delete <name>?" dialog (types with documents offer "Archive" instead).
Click "Save changes" in the page header; a "Settings saved." toast confirms.
prerequisites: User holds the exact permission marketing_review.workflows.write_all and the document type library loads (the tab is hidden otherwise).

workflows.title: How to move a project card through the review kanban board
workflows.purpose: Show how a project card advances across the Marketing Projects board columns ("Submitter review" > "Admin review" > "Resolved") by approving its document from the document review page; cards are not dragged, they move as document statuses change.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects; the "Marketing Projects" board shows the columns "Submitter review", "Admin review" and "Resolved" (plus a drafts column when drafts exist).
Locate a project card in the "Admin review" column whose badge indicates it is in your queue (the header info tooltip explains "Step X • For my review").
Click the card (or open its "..." menu and choose "View project") to open the "Project details page".
In the documents table, click "View" on the document row to open the document review page.
Review the document, then click the approver action button titled "Approve Document" in the review toolbar.
In the "Approve document" dialog, optionally add an "Approval note (optional)" and click "Approve document".
Navigate back to Marketing > Projects and confirm the card has moved to "Resolved" (final approval on every document) or remains in "Admin review" with its badge advanced to the next step.
prerequisites: A project with one processed document sitting at an approver step where the recording user is an eligible approver (card in the "Admin review" column).
User is a marketing approver (approver actions render only for approvers on the review page).
suggestedSetupSteps: Create a project via Marketing > Projects > "New" with a single-step workflow whose approval group includes the recording user; after AI processing completes the card sits in "Admin review".

workflows.title: How to add context to Firm Intelligence
workflows.purpose: Add firm context (a pasted text source, uploaded file or link) to Firm Intelligence from the Intelligence composer, watch the sources get processed into findings in a new chat thread, and save a finding to the context library.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Intelligence; the page greets you ("Happy <weekday>, <name>") with the composer "Ask about your firm's context, or provide context via file, link, or text…".
Click the round "+" button (aria-label "Add context", tooltip "Add context — upload files, paste text, or add links") at the bottom-left of the composer.
Choose "Add text source" from the menu (the other options are "Upload file" and "Paste link").
In the "Paste long text content" dialog, paste or type the policy text and click "Add long text"; a context card appears staged under the composer.
Click the round arrow "Submit" button (aria-label "Submit") to add the context; a new chat is created and you are redirected to /marketing/intelligence/chats/<id>.
In the thread, the source-add turn shows the tabs "Answer", "Findings" and "Steps" with a processing stepper; wait until findings appear as cards on the "Answer" tab.
On a finding card, click "Save context"; a "Context saved." toast with a "View Library" action confirms it was added to the library.
Optionally ask a follow-up or add more context in the thread composer ("Ask a follow-up, or add more context…").
