workflows.title: How to edit or manage a Firm Intelligence finding
workflows.purpose: Open the Manage Context library, drill into a source's findings, and edit, save, archive or delete an individual finding from its detail panel.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Intelligence, then click the layers icon link labelled "Manage context" (tooltip) in the Intelligence header to open the "Manage Context" page.
Optionally filter with the "Search sources..." field, then click a source row (title plus a "Findings" count badge) to expand its accordion.
In the findings table ("Finding Name", "Last updated", "Status", "Classification"), click the view action (aria-label "View finding") on a row; the finding detail panel opens on the right.
Click "Edit" in the panel to open the "Edit finding" dialog ("Update the source title or the finding content before saving.").
Change the title input and/or the finding text and click "Save changes"; a "Finding updated." toast confirms.
For a finding still in review, click "Save Context" to mark it completed ("Context saved." toast); a completed finding offers "Archive" instead, and an archived one "Unarchive".
To remove a finding still in review, click "Delete", then "Delete" in the "Delete finding?" dialog; a "Finding deleted." toast confirms and the panel closes.
prerequisites: Company has the context_iq feature ACTIVE and the user passes useCanAccessContextIQ.
At least one source with extracted findings in the context library (the "Delete" and "Save Context" buttons appear only for findings with status ready_for_review).
suggestedSetupSteps: Run the 'How to add context to Firm Intelligence' flow first (add a text source and wait for findings) so a source with findings exists; leave at least one finding unsaved so "Save Context"/"Delete" are available.

workflows.title: How to reopen a closed exception in Account surveillance
workflows.purpose: Find a closed (or escalated) exception on the Account surveillance overview, open its detail page, and reopen it with a required reason so it returns to the Open review queue.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview

Scroll to the "Exceptions" table and click the "Closed" filter chip (the chips are "All", "Open", "New", "Escalated", "Closed", "Archived") to list resolved exceptions; rows show a "Resolved" status badge.
Click the exception row (or its Case ID link) to open the exception detail page.
In the page header, click "Reopen exception" (this button only appears when the exception is not Open).
In the "Reopen exception" dialog ("This exception will move from Closed back to Open."), type the rationale in the "Reason for reopening" field.
Click "Reopen exception" to confirm.
Verify the "Exception reopened" toast, that the "Review status" badge in the right rail now reads "Open", and that the header again shows the "Escalate" and "Close" buttons.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company (company feature "trade_surveillance") and the user has access to it (useCanAccessTradeSurveillance); otherwise the page shows the ModuleAccessView upsell.
At least one exception in Closed or Escalated status (the "Reopen exception" button only renders when status is not Open).
suggestedSetupSteps: Exceptions only exist once trade data has been ingested: either a custodian feed is connected (Account surveillance > Feed monitor) or a CSV/XLSX is uploaded at /account-surveillance/import_data for a configured custodian.

With trades present, create an exception either by running a rule (Overview > "Rule library" > row menu > "Run now") or manually: Account surveillance > Trades, tick one or more trade rows, click "Create manual exception", fill "Title", pick a severity, and click "Create exception".
Open the new exception and click "Close" in the header, pick a "Determination", fill "Resolution summary", and click "Close exception" so there is a closed exception to reopen.

workflows.title: How to archive a flagged exception
workflows.purpose: Archive a surveillance exception from its detail page with a required audit reason, hiding it from the active queue while keeping it in the audit trail (with the option to unarchive later).
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
In the "Exceptions" table, click the exception row you want to archive to open its detail page.
Click the red "Archive" button in the page header (only visible to admins).

In the "Archive exception" dialog, read the warning alert (for a live, non-sandbox flag it says the flag "leaves the review queue for everyone") and type the explanation in the "Archive reason" field.
Click "Yes, archive this live flag" (the button reads "Archive exception" when the flag is sandbox output) to confirm.
Verify the "Flag archived" toast, the "This flag is archived" banner at the top of the page showing who archived it and the reason, and that the header button now reads "Unarchive".
Optionally return to Account surveillance > Overview and click the "Archived" filter chip: the exception appears with an "Archived" status badge and an "Archive reason" column.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user.
User must be an admin (useIsAdmin) — the "Archive"/"Unarchive" header button and the bulk "Archive" action are admin-only.
At least one exception (any status) that is not already archived.
suggestedSetupSteps: Ensure trade data exists (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX upload at /account-surveillance/import_data).

Create an exception via a rule run (Overview > "Rule library" > row menu > "Run now") or manually from Account surveillance > Trades: tick trade rows, click "Create manual exception", fill "Title", choose a severity, click "Create exception".

workflows.title: How to save and reuse a custom trade search
workflows.purpose: Apply filters on the Trades blotter, save them as a named saved search from the "Trade filters" panel, and reapply them later from the "Saved searches" dropdown.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Trades

In the table toolbar, click "Filters" to open the "Trade filters" side panel (sections: "Saved search", "Date and time", "Executed by", "Account", "Security", "Value"; a "Representative" section also appears when reps do not share all clients).

Set your criteria — for example expand "Security" and type a ticker in "Symbol", and expand "Date and time" and click the "Last 30 days" chip. Filters apply to the table immediately; the "Filters" button shows a count of active filters.
Expand the "Saved search" section, type a name in "Filter name" (placeholder "e.g. Large option sells") and optionally a "Description".
Click "Save as new". The saved search becomes the selected search in the "Saved search" dropdown.
To reuse it later, on the Trades page open the "Saved searches" dropdown in the table toolbar and pick the saved search by name — its filters are reapplied to the table.
To change a saved search, adjust the filters while it is selected and click "Update saved" in the "Saved search" section.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user.
Some trades ingested (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX import) so the filtered table has rows to show — saving a search itself does not require trades.

workflows.title: How to escalate a flagged compliance exception
workflows.purpose: Escalate an open surveillance exception from its detail page with a required escalation reason so it is marked Escalated and surfaced to the compliance team; optionally assign a reviewer from the right rail.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
In the "Exceptions" table (default chip "Open"), click an exception row with a "New" status badge to open its detail page.
Optionally, in the right rail under "Assigned to", pick the reviewer from the person dropdown (options are "Unassigned" plus admin names); the change saves immediately.
Click "Escalate" in the page header.

In the "Escalate exception" dialog, read the warning ("This exception will be marked as escalated and surfaced to the compliance team. It can be reopened later if needed.") and type the justification in the "Escalation reason" field.
Click "Escalate exception" to submit.
Verify the "Exception escalated" toast, that "Review status" now shows "Escalated", and that the header now shows "Reopen exception" instead of "Escalate"/"Close".
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user.
At least one exception in Open status (the "Escalate" button only renders while status is Open).
suggestedSetupSteps: Ensure trade data exists (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX upload at /account-surveillance/import_data).

Create an open exception via a rule run (Overview > "Rule library" > row menu > "Run now") or manually from Account surveillance > Trades: tick trade rows, click "Create manual exception", fill "Title", choose a severity, click "Create exception".

workflows.title: How to close a flagged compliance exception
workflows.purpose: Review an open surveillance exception's detail page and close it by recording a determination and a resolution summary that are stored in the audit trail.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
In the "Exceptions" table, click an exception row with a "New" status badge to open its detail page.

Review the "What happened" summary alert, the "Rule type" and "Generated" details, the trades and parties cards, and the activity trail; the right rail shows "Review status", "Severity" and "Assigned to".
Click "Close" in the page header.

In the "Close exception" dialog ("Confirm no further action is required after review."), open the "Determination" select (placeholder "Select determination") and pick an option such as "No violation · within firm policy" or "Violation confirmed · internal remediation".
Type the review findings in the "Resolution summary" field (required).
Click "Close exception" to confirm.
Verify the "Exception closed" toast and that "Review status" now reads "Closed"; back on the Overview the exception is listed under the "Closed" chip with a "Resolved" badge.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user.
At least one exception in Open status (the "Close" button only renders while status is Open).
suggestedSetupSteps: Ensure trade data exists (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX upload at /account-surveillance/import_data).

Create an open exception via a rule run (Overview > "Rule library" > row menu > "Run now") or manually from Account surveillance > Trades: tick trade rows, click "Create manual exception", fill "Title", choose a severity, click "Create exception".

workflows.title: How to bulk close multiple flagged exceptions at once
workflows.purpose: An admin selects several exceptions in the Overview "Exceptions" table and closes them together with a single audit reason via the bulk action bar.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview

In the "Exceptions" table, optionally narrow the list with the status chips ("All", "Open", "New", "Escalated", "Closed", "Archived"), the "Filter by rule" multi-select, or the "Search exceptions..." search.
Tick the checkbox at the start of each exception row you want to close (row selection is only available to admins).

A bulk action bar appears above the table reading "N flags selected" with the actions "Close", "Escalate", "Reopen", "Archive", a "Set severity" select, an "Assign to" select and "Clear". Click "Close".

In the "Close flags" dialog ("Applies to N selected flags. This can be changed later from the flag detail page."), type a summary in the "Reason" field (required; stored in the audit record for each flag).
Click "Close N flags" (e.g. "Close 3 flags") to confirm.
Wait for the dialog to close and the selection to clear; the closed exceptions drop out of the "Open" view and appear under the "Closed" chip with a "Resolved" status badge.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user.
User must be an admin (useIsAdmin) — row checkboxes and the bulk action bar render only for admins.
At least two exceptions in Open or Escalated status.
suggestedSetupSteps: Ensure trade data exists (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX upload at /account-surveillance/import_data).

Generate several exceptions by running a rule (Overview > "Rule library" > row menu > "Run now"), or create two or more manual exceptions from Account surveillance > Trades (tick trades > "Create manual exception" > "Title" + severity > "Create exception").

workflows.title: How to import trade and holdings data
workflows.purpose: Upload a CSV or XLSX of trades and holdings for a configured custodian on the Import data page so the records are ingested for surveillance processing.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview, then go directly to the URL /account-surveillance/import_data (the "Import data" page is not linked from the sidebar).

Under "Custodian", open the dropdown (placeholder "Select a custodian") and pick the custodian matching your file. If only one custodian is configured it is pre-selected and the dropdown is disabled with the note "Only one custodian configuration available".
Under "Input CSV/XLSX", click the file input (enabled once a custodian is selected) and choose a .csv or .xlsx file; any other type shows an "Invalid file type" toast.
Click "Upload and Proceed" (it shows "Uploading..." while in flight).
Confirm the "Upload successful" toast ("Trades are processing."); the file input clears.
Optionally navigate to Account surveillance > Feed monitor or Trades to see the ingested records once processing finishes.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user.
At least one trade data config (custodian) exists for the tenant (useTradeDataConfigs); with none configured the dropdown is empty and the upload cannot proceed.
A CSV/XLSX fixture formatted to that custodian's expected layout.
suggestedSetupSteps: Custodian trade-data configs are not created in the UI; have the tenant's custodian config provisioned (backend/CS) before recording.
Prepare a small CSV in that custodian's format containing a few trades and holdings.

workflows.title: How to create a new surveillance rule from a template
workflows.purpose: Open the Rule library from the Account surveillance overview, pick a rule template (Front running shown), and complete the step-by-step wizard to name, configure, scope, and publish the rule.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
Click "Rule library" in the page header to open the "Rules" page.
Click "Create new rule" in the Rules page header to open the "Rules configuration" page ("Select a rule template").
Optionally type in "Search for templates by name or keyword"; then on the "Front running" card (under "Trading practices & order handling") click "Use this template".

The "Front running" wizard opens with a left stepper: "Configure parameters" ("Name & overview", "Detection parameters", "Security matching", "Pattern & escalation", "Accounts & groups", "Activation & severity") and "Review & publish". In "Name & overview", type a "Rule name" and optionally a "Description".
Click "Next" and review the defaults on "Detection parameters", "Security matching" and "Pattern & escalation", clicking "Next" after each.

On "Accounts & groups", the account types ("Employee personal accounts", "Client accounts", "Firm accounts") are locked for this template; optionally pick groups under "Exclude employee groups (optional)", then click "Next".

On "Activation & severity", under "Status after publish" choose "Activate on publish", "Inactive on publish" or "Sandbox", and under "Default severity" choose "High", "Moderate" or "Low"; click "Next".
On "Review & publish", check the summary side panel, then click "Publish" in the page header (enabled only on this step; "Save as draft" is disabled).
Verify the "Rule published" toast and that you are returned to the "Rules" list where the new rule appears with its "Status" badge ("Active", "Sandbox" or "Inactive").
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and accessible to the user (the "Rule library" header button is hidden otherwise).

workflows.title: How to edit a surveillance rule's configuration
workflows.purpose: Open an existing surveillance rule in its template wizard, change its name, thresholds, activation status, or severity, and republish it.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview, then click "Rule library" in the page header (this opens the "Rules" page at /account-surveillance/rules)
In the rules table, find the rule to change and click the vertical "..." (more) button at the right end of its row
Click "Edit" in the dropdown menu (alternatively, click the row to open the rule's details page and click "Edit rule" in its header)

The rule opens in its template wizard (for example a Front running rule shows the page title "Front running" with a left-hand stepper: "Configure parameters" with sub-steps "Name & overview", "Detection parameters", "Security matching", "Pattern & escalation", "Accounts & groups", "Activation & severity", then "Review & publish"); the header shows "Cancel", "Save as draft" (disabled) and "Publish" (disabled until the review step)
On "Name & overview", update the "Rule name" and/or "Description" fields
Click "Next" to move through the parameter steps and adjust thresholds as needed (fields vary by template)
On "Activation & severity", choose "Status after publish" ("Activate on publish", "Inactive on publish", or "Sandbox") and a "Default severity" ("High", "Moderate", or "Low")
Click "Next" until you reach "Review & publish", then click "Publish" in the header
A "Rule updated" toast appears and you are redirected to the rule's details page, where the "How this rule operates" section reflects the new "Status" and "Default severity level"
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company (feature "trade_surveillance") and the user has trade surveillance access
At least one existing surveillance rule that is not a Cross trading rule (Cross trading rules open a "Cross trading unavailable" notice instead of an editor)
suggestedSetupSteps: Go to /account-surveillance/rules and click "Create new rule" in the header
Pick a template (e.g. Front running), complete the wizard steps (only "Rule name" is required on the first step; other steps have defaults) and click "Publish" on the "Review & publish" step

workflows.title: How to activate, deactivate, or sandbox a surveillance rule
workflows.purpose: Switch a surveillance rule between Active, Inactive, and Sandbox deployment states from the rules table without opening the full editor.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview, then click "Rule library" in the page header to open the "Rules" page
Locate the target rule in the table and note its current badge in the "Status" column ("Active", "Sandbox", or "Inactive")
Click the vertical "..." (more) button at the right end of the rule's row
If the rule is not active, click "Activate" in the dropdown; a "Rule updated" toast ("Rule activated successfully") appears and the "Status" badge changes to "Active"
If the rule is active, click "Deactivate" in the dropdown to open the "Deactivate Rule" dialog ("Choose how you'd like to deactivate this rule:")

Click the "Inactive" option to fully disable the rule, or the "Sandbox" option to keep it running without notifications and with alerts marked as "Sandbox" (or click "Cancel" to close without changes)
A "Rule updated" toast confirms the change ("Rule set to inactive successfully" or "Rule set to sandbox successfully") and the "Status" badge updates
Optionally click the "Active", "Sandbox", or "Inactive" filter chips above the table to show only rules in that state
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and user has trade surveillance access
At least one existing surveillance rule that is not a Cross trading rule (Cross trading rules cannot be activated or sandboxed; a "Cross trading unavailable" toast appears)
suggestedSetupSteps: Go to /account-surveillance/rules and click "Create new rule", choose a template, complete the wizard and click "Publish"

workflows.title: How to manually run a surveillance rule
workflows.purpose: Queue an on-demand run of a rule outside its normal schedule and land on the resulting rule run's results page.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview, then click "Rule library" in the page header to open the "Rules" page
Click the vertical "..." (more) button at the right end of the target rule's row
Click "Run now" in the dropdown menu
A "Rule run queued" toast appears ("The rule is now queued and should start in a few seconds.") and you are redirected to /account-surveillance/rule_runs/<id>

While the run is queued the page shows "Waiting for the rule run to start (usually takes a few seconds), this page will automatically refresh when the run has started...", then "Running rule (usually takes a few seconds)..." while it is pending

When complete, the page titled "<Rule name> - Results" shows the run summary ("Start date/time", "End date/time", "Status", "Rule", "Accounts", "Trades", "Holdings", "Clients", "Representatives", "Alerts", "Severity", "Rule status") and the "Alerts for this run" table

workflows.title: How to view a rule run's results
workflows.purpose: Open a completed rule run to inspect its status, the volume of data processed, and the alerts it generated.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
Click "Rule runs" in the page header to open the "All rule runs" page (/account-surveillance/rule_runs)

In the runs table (columns "Rule triggered", "Status", "Complete date/time", "Accounts", "Trades", "Holdings", "Clients", "Representatives", "Is sandbox", "Alerts"), click the "Status" badge or the "Complete date/time" value of the run you want to inspect (alternatively, on the "Rules" page click the timestamp in a rule's "Last run" column)

The results page titled "<Rule name> - Results" opens; review the summary rows "Start date/time", "End date/time", "Status", "Rule", "Accounts", "Trades", "Holdings", "Clients", "Representatives", "Alerts", "Severity", and "Rule status"
Optionally click the rule name link next to "Rule" (with the external-link icon) to open the rule's details page in a new tab
Scroll to the "Alerts for this run" section to see the alerts table for this run
Click an alert row to open that alert's detail page
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and user has trade surveillance access
At least one completed rule run (created by a scheduled run or by "Run now" on a rule)
For the alerts table to have rows, the run must have produced alerts, which requires ingested trade/holdings data that trips the rule
suggestedSetupSteps: Go to /account-surveillance/rules, open a rule's "..." menu and click "Run now"; wait for the run to complete

workflows.title: How to view and link entities in the Client Relationship Builder graph
workflows.purpose: Open the Company structure graph to see how the firm, representatives, clients, and accounts are connected, and draw a new relationship edge between two nodes.
steps: Navigate directly to /account-surveillance/company_structure (the page is titled "Company structure" and is not linked from the Account surveillance sidebar)
Wait for the "Loading relationship data..." indicator to disappear; the "Client Relationship Builder" card ("Visualize and manage client-company relationships.") shows the graph canvas
Use the graph controls in the bottom-left of the canvas to zoom in/out or fit the view and locate the source and target nodes (nodes are labelled with the entity's display name)
Drag from the connection handle at the bottom of the source node to the handle at the top of the target node
Release on the target node; a "Creating relationship..." indicator appears in the bottom-right corner while the edge is saved
Confirm the new edge is drawn between the two nodes on the canvas
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and user has trade surveillance access

Relationship graph data must exist: at least a company node plus representatives/clients/accounts, which come from ingested trade/holdings data (custodian feed or the Import data upload); otherwise the page shows "No relationship data found."
suggestedSetupSteps: Go to /account-surveillance/import_data, choose a "Custodian", pick a CSV/XLSX file under "Input CSV/XLSX" and click "Upload and Proceed" so representatives, clients and accounts exist
Return to /account-surveillance/company_structure once processing has finished

workflows.title: How to search and filter representatives
workflows.purpose: Find representatives by first or last name and narrow the list to active or inactive representatives.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Representatives
Type at least two characters of a representative's first or last name into the "Search first or last name..." field; the table filters after a short delay
Click the "Active" chip in the toolbar above the table to show only active representatives
Click the "Inactive" chip to show only inactive representatives
Click the "All statuses" chip to clear the status filter
Click the "X" button that appears to the right of the search field to clear the search text
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and user has trade surveillance access
At least one representative record exists (representatives come from ingested trade/holdings data or the Import data upload)
suggestedSetupSteps: If no representatives exist, go to /account-surveillance/import_data, choose a "Custodian", select a CSV/XLSX under "Input CSV/XLSX" and click "Upload and Proceed"

workflows.title: How to monitor incoming data feed sync status
workflows.purpose: Review custodian data feed sync records and filter them by source, status, and file type to spot failed or missing imports.
steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Feed monitor
Review the table columns "Source", "Sync date", "Status", "File type", and "Filename"
Type into the "Search source, status, or filename..." field to filter rows by matching text
Use the "All sources" dropdown in the toolbar to quickly restrict the list to one data feed source
Click "Filters" to open the "Feed filters" side panel
In the "Source" section, pick a source from the "All sources" dropdown
In the "Status" section, pick a status from the "All statuses" dropdown (the available values are taken from the existing sync records)
In the "File type" section, pick a type from the "All file types" dropdown; the table updates as each selection is made and the "Filters" button shows a count of active filters
Click the "Close filters" (X) button in the panel header to close the panel
To reset, clear the search text with the "X" next to the search field and set each dropdown back to its "All ..." option
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company and user has trade surveillance access
At least one external sync record exists, i.e. a connected custodian feed (e.g. Schwab, Pershing, Apex S3, SFTP direct upload) has delivered files; without syncs the table and dropdowns are empty
workflows.blockerReason: Sync records (ExternalSync) are produced by backend feed ingestion from custodian/SFTP sources; the UI offers no way to create one (the Import data page uploads trade files but the code does not show it creating a feed-monitor sync record).
